limits: Native acceptance combines the full run, four overlapping fixture corrections and two overlapping click regressions: 88 unique tests, not summed run totals. The original three native failures remain recorded.
The first 117-stage Shipping run failed 14 assertions on BE72701B and is retained as superseded evidence; only the later clean run establishes Shipping interaction acceptance.

The prior F9 executable had one GPU display-startup crash at zero seconds, device-removed reason -2005270522 with no DRED breadcrumb data. Its unchanged four-state retry passed and is archived separately from final 0A8AB4BC display evidence. No root cause or fix is established and recurrence remains possible.
Benchmark files are complete report evidence; they do not embed an executable hash. The package hash is read separately, and the launching wrapper checks report freshness.
Short isolated views with a fresh core and empty neighbors do not establish crowded-colony or long-session performance.
CPU/GPU counters may lag rendered frames; timing channels are not a synchronized queue trace.
Visible/near coverage counters track conservative CPU cell residency, not GPU upload fences or pixel coverage. Zero initial waits can mean cells were resident from prior views.
Travel and orbit retain live streaming; sector focus changes can include terrain/forest rebuilds, not grass cost alone.
Foliage handoffs, terrain patterns, stylized Rex and native-resolution responsiveness remain visual/performance limitations. No sustained 60 FPS or Manor Lords parity is claimed.
Endpoint sampling is bounded observation, not packet capture or proof of all future network behavior.

Post-check user report and source audit confirm aggregate worker visuals and population-independent courier creation; v0.8.1 retains this model. Individual persistent worker identities are planned for v0.9.

Post-check source audit found a floating-point contact-radius stall in melee enemy movement; a focused fix/regression is planned for v0.9. Friendly structures intentionally block current 2D fire lines.
